If you are to write about a loli, you must not write only about a loli
You must write about the morning light climbing over her sleep-mussed chestnut short hair, the fine soft strands clinging to her faintly sweat-damp forehead; write about how, half awake, she whimpers and burrows into your arms, and how the arms she wraps around you carry a childlike dependence and an unquestionable possessiveness
You must write about her wearing an apron clearly too big for her, standing on a small stool and clattering as she prepares breakfast. Amid the sizzle of the spatula and the frying egg is mixed her tuneless, chirping humming
Write about how she curls up in a corner of the sofa reading in the afternoon, her little feet dangling and swinging, the two cat patterns on the toes of her socks nodding along.
Write about how, when you come home exhausted, she runs over to take your bag, lifts her face, her eyes filled with utter joy and understanding, and says those magic words: \u201cYou\u2019re back\u2014thank you for working so hard.\u201d Her voice is sweet and clear, yet carries a certainty that can smooth out every crease
You must write about how, when she is angry, her slightly puffed cheeks look like they hold a pinecone, yet she can explain things more clearly than you can.
